summary: Povidone-iodine 5% (0.5% available iodine) is an OTC topical antiseptic used as first aid to help prevent infection in minor cuts, scrapes, and burns. It releases free iodine that broadly kills bacteria, fungi, viruses, and protozoa; it is for external use only and limited to short-term use.
indications: First aid to help prevent infection in minor cuts, scrapes, and burns
Topical antiseptic for skin disinfection (e.g. minor wound and pre-procedure skin antisepsis)

dosage.c: Minor cuts, scrapes, burns (first aid antiseptic)
dosage.d: Clean the affected area; spray a small amount on the area 1 to 3 times daily
dosage.t: Short-term; do not use longer than 1 week without medical advice
dosage.n: May be covered with a sterile bandage; if bandaged, let dry first

admin: Clean the affected area before applying
Spray a small amount of product on the area 1 to 3 times daily
May be covered with a sterile bandage; if bandaged, let it dry first
Do not use in the eyes or over large areas of the body
moa: Povidone-iodine is an iodophor that slowly liberates free molecular iodine on contact with skin and mucosa. Free iodine penetrates microbial cell walls and oxidizes key amino acids, nucleotides, and fatty acids, denaturing proteins and enzymes and killing a broad spectrum of bacteria, fungi, viruses, and protozoa.

absolute: Allergy to povidone-iodine or any ingredient in the preparation
relative: Use over large areas of the body
Deep or puncture wounds, serious burns, or animal bites without medical advice
Use for more than 1 week without medical advice
monitor: Stop use and ask a doctor if the condition persists or worsens
Stop use if used for more than 1 week

preg: Ask a doctor before use if pregnant. Although topical, iodine can be systemically absorbed (especially over large or broken areas) and may affect fetal/neonatal thyroid function; avoid prolonged or extensive use during pregnancy.
lact: Ask a doctor before use if breastfeeding. Iodine can be absorbed and may pass into breast milk and affect infant thyroid function; avoid extensive or prolonged use during lactation.

moderate: Other topical antiseptics, especially hydrogen peroxide and silver-/mercury-containing products (chemical incompatibility, may reduce efficacy)
interactions.diagnostics: Iodine absorption may interfere with thyroid function tests and radioactive iodine uptake studies; may cause false readings in some occult-blood and other assays.

serious: Thyroid dysfunction with extensive or prolonged use (iodine absorption)
rare: Chemical burn or irritation with prolonged occlusive contact
emergency: Iodine toxicity from ingestion or massive absorption

monitoring: Watch for local irritation or allergic reaction at the application site
No routine monitoring for short-term OTC first-aid use
Consider thyroid function with extensive or prolonged use, especially in neonates
counsel: Do not use in the eyes or over large areas of the body
Do not use if allergic to povidone-iodine or any ingredient
Ask a doctor before use for deep or puncture wounds, serious burns, or animal bites
Stop use and ask a doctor if the condition persists or worsens or if you need it for more than 1 week
Keep out of reach of children; if swallowed, get medical help or contact a Poison Control Center right away
Product may stain skin and fabric
pearls: Contains povidone-iodine 5% which equals 0.5% available iodine; the povidone carrier releases free iodine gradually, giving broad-spectrum, sustained germicidal activity with less irritation than free iodine.
Many record fields (renal/hepatic dose adjustment, plasma pharmacokinetics) are not applicable for a topical antiseptic.
Avoid routine use on large surface areas, deep wounds, or in neonates because absorbed iodine can affect thyroid function.
Effective for pre-procedure skin antisepsis; allow it to dry to achieve full antimicrobial effect.
Limit OTC use to one week; persistent wounds need medical evaluation.
missed: Not applicable - used as needed for first aid rather than on a fixed dosing schedule. Apply when treating the affected area, up to 1 to 3 times daily.
overdose: Topical use is low risk. If swallowed, get medical help or contact a Poison Control Center right away. Excessive or prolonged application over large or broken skin can cause systemic iodine absorption with possible thyroid dysfunction, metabolic disturbance, and (rarely) corrosive mucosal injury after ingestion; management is supportive.
